consistency_note: No. Landscape POV is zero, so there is no journey to be consistent with. The two landscape train clips are both underground platform shots (no city, no daylight) from different stations and different rolling stock. The five countable landscape landmark clips are ALL timelapses (Eiffel x2, Arc de Triomphe x2, Seine x1): four are summer daytime with cumulus skies and would sit together, but one Arc clip runs dusk-to-night, and none is real-time footage, so they will not match real-time train footage. The single POV clip (vertical, bare autumn/winter trees) clashes in season with the summer landmarks.
sourcing_note: Hard. 10 site-restricted searches returned the same 2-3 Paris metro clips over and over. Worked: "view from train window Paris" (found the one Bir-Hakeim POV clip), "paris metro train", landmark names (Eiffel, Arc de Triomphe, Seine, Louvre return plenty). Found nothing for: RER, tramway, Gare du Nord / Gare de Lyon / TGV / SNCF, elevated metro seen from the street or drone, Montmartre, Notre-Dame. Generic "train window" results were all other places (Kuala Lumpur, New York, Chicago, a mountain city, North American LRT): 10 of 21 viewed clips were wrong-city. Not found at all: any landscape >=1080p Paris train POV; any above-ground Paris train exterior. TOOLING: fetch_pexels.sh failed to resolve every id above ~26,000,000 that was tried (0 of 21 across both cities) plus two older clips with nonstandard dimensions, so recent uploads could not be measured at all - the totals are a floor for landmarks, and newer train clips may exist unmeasured. pipeline/audit/sheet.sh crashes with this ffmpeg 6.1.1 (pad filter error on every clip), so frame sheets were made with an equivalent scratch script (4 frames per clip at 10/37/63/90%); the repo script was not modified. Steadiness is judged from stills, not from playback.
